title: feat(spec): rule and enforce submitBehavior.url — relative-only, declared-field interpolation, URL-escaped (#7496)
body:
Fixes #7496

## What was ruled

The maintainer ruling recorded on #7496 (2026-08-11, quoted verbatim and untranslated):

> **Ruling: narrowest shape.** `submitBehavior.url` accepts:
> - **relative paths only** — absolute URLs are refused (closes the open-redirect face);
> - **interpolation only from declared record fields**, and every interpolated value is **URL-escaped**;
> - a verbatim redirect on the resolved relative path IS the intended consumption.
>
> Widen later iff measured demand appears (e.g. an allowlist of absolute origins) — not before. Spec side documents AND enforces this shape in the schema; objectui#4190's consumer hardening is scoped after this lands.

## Premise verification against `origin/main`

Re-verified at `8c20f75`, after today's #7585/#7487 merges touched this file. The premise held exactly as filed:

- The landing site is where the card said: the FormView `submitBehavior` discriminated union's `redirect` arm in `packages/spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts`.
- `url` was `z.string()` with **no describe and no constraint at all**. So `https://example.com/thanks`, `//evil.example`, `javascript:alert(1)` and the empty string all parsed today — this change is an **acceptance-surface narrowing**, which is why the changeset is a `major` for `@objectstack/spec`.
- The batch18 pins (`view-strictness-batch18.test.ts:184/218/333`) all spell `url: '/x'` or `'/done'`, i.e. already-conforming relative paths. No pin needed rewriting; all 129 cases across view-strictness + error-map still pass unchanged.

## Interpolation syntax — measured, not assumed

The card flagged the token grammar as UNMEASURED. Measurement, all in `packages/spec`:

| Dialect | Where it lives | Verdict for this key |
|---|---|---|
| Double-brace `{{record.x}}` / `{{os.user.id}}` — the ADR-0032 §3 text template, CEL variable scope | `shared/expression.zod.ts` (`tmpl`, `TemplateExpressionInputSchema`) | **adopted**, narrowed twice |
| Double-brace `{{page.var}}` | `ui/action.zod.ts` `bodyExtra`, resolved by `resolvePageVarTokens` | wrong scope for a post-submit redirect |
| Dollar-brace `${param.X}` / `${ctx.X}` | `ui/action.zod.ts:892` action `target` | a fourth spelling; not adopted |
| Single-brace `{current_user_id}` context tokens, single-brace flow `{var}` | `data/context-tokens.zod.ts`, `automation/flow-node-expression-paths.ts` | different vocabularies; refused here |

So a grammar **does** exist and this key did not need a new one. `{{record.field_name}}` is the platform's own double-brace dialect, narrowed twice against it because a redirect target has a much smaller honest scope than a notification body: only the `record.` root (the record just submitted is all the post-submit moment has), and only a **flat** field segment in the same lowercase snake_case grammar `object.fields` keys are declared under (`data/object.zod.ts:1593`). A token that could never name a field is refused at the door rather than substituted into a URL.

## What is enforced, and what deliberately is not

Parse time knows the *string*; it does not know the *object*. Split accordingly:

- **Enforced here (parse-time decidable).** Relative-only, with each hazard refused by its own message: absolute (any `scheme:`, so `javascript:` and `data:` come along), protocol-relative `//host`, backslash (browsers normalise it to `/`, so `/\host` leaves the origin exactly like `//host`), whitespace and control characters (browsers strip them before resolving, which is how a leading-slash check gets walked past), document-relative `thanks` / `./thanks`, and the empty string. Plus token-grammar validity — any brace shape that is not `{{record.field_name}}`.
- **NOT enforced here — and where it belongs.** Whether `{{record.foo}}` names a field this form's object actually **declares** needs both the string and the object, which the Zod schema does not have. That belongs to the reference-integrity family in `@objectstack/lint` (`validate-page-field-bindings.ts`, `reference-integrity-suite.ts`, `validate-expressions.ts`), which already resolves field references against object declarations. It is out of scope for this card and is not filed as a defect: nothing regresses by its absence, since before this PR the whole key was unvalidated.
- **NOT enforceable here — the URL-escaping half of bullet 2** is a consumer obligation. It is stated in the describe, in the forms guide, and handed to objectui#4190.

## Cross-face conclusions — one line per url-consuming face

⚠️ No silent skips; every face I found is listed.

| Face | Conclusion |
|---|---|
| `FormView.submitBehavior` `redirect` arm `url` | **CHANGED** — this PR. |
| The `thank-you` / `continue` / `next-record` sibling arms | **Already conformant** — none carries a `url` or any address-shaped key; pinned as a regression guard in section 5 of the new test file. |
| Wizard success behavior | **Already conformant by reuse, not by a second schema.** There is no separate wizard success-behavior schema — grep for `successBehavior` / `onComplete` / `completeBehavior` in `packages/spec/src` returns nothing. A wizard step embeds a FormView (`examples/app-showcase/src/ui/pages/new-project-wizard.page.ts:42` authors `submitBehavior` inside one), and the liveness ledger records objectui's `WizardForm.tsx:315-316` dispatching the same four kinds as `ObjectForm` (`packages/spec/liveness/view.json:330-332`). One schema, so the ruling reaches the wizard path with no second edit. |
| `UrlNavItem.url` (`ui/app.zod.ts:525`) | **Explicitly out of scope** — declared "Target external URL", and its own type-assertion fixture authors `https://example.com` (`ui/app.nav-type-assertions.ts:112`). Linking OUT of the app is the whole capability; narrowing it would delete it. This is also where the new refusal messages **point** an author who genuinely wants an external destination. |
| `DashboardHeaderAction.actionUrl` (`ui/dashboard.zod.ts:89`) | **Explicitly out of scope** — "URL **or target** for the action", paired with `actionType`, so the value is not always an address. Not a post-submit redirect and not fed by record data; the ruling does not reach it. |
| `Action.target` (`ui/action.zod.ts:892`) | **Explicitly out of scope** — "URL, Script Name, Flow ID, or API Endpoint" across every action type, with its own `${param.X}` dialect. Ruling this would be a separate decision on a much wider key. |
| `SharingConfig.publicLink` (`ui/sharing.zod.ts:95`) | **Explicitly out of scope** — a generated share slug, not an author-supplied navigation target. |

## Where the ruling is written down

The describe on `url` states all three bullets in full, and reaches the generated JSON Schema (7 occurrences in `objectstack.json`, the machine-readable contract authoring tools read).

⚠️ One honest correction to the card's expectation: it does **not** reach `content/docs/references/ui/view.mdx`, because that page renders a union as one type expression and gives a union member's inner key no row. So the headline also rides on the `submitBehavior` describe, which **does** have a row there — that is the one-line diff in the regenerated reference. The human-facing home for the full rules is a new subsection in `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx` §8 with accepted/refused examples, plus a renderer-status note in the shape of the existing #7245 one (the console still redirects verbatim, so a token would reach the browser literally until objectui#4190 lands).

## Tests

New file `packages/spec/src/ui/view-submit-redirect-url.test.ts` — 52 cases. Every refusal case asserts the **message** an author reads (the rule it names, the reason, the prescribed fix, and the ruling date so the refusal is traceable), never a bare parse failure. Acceptance is pinned as hard as refusal, because a relative-only rule written slightly too tight is indistinguishable from a correct one until a legitimate `/thanks?ref=` + a record token stops parsing.

**Reverse verification** — direction predicted before running: **RED for the refusal half only**, and green-throughout for the acceptance half, because a pure narrowing cannot move a case that was accepted before. Probe taken out with a checkpoint commit plus a path-scoped `git checkout HEAD` restore — never `git stash`. Measured: with the `superRefine` removed, **33 of 94** cases go red — every refusal case plus the issue-path/code pin — while all acceptance cases and all of `view-strictness-batch18` stay green. Restored; 129/129 green again.

## Gates run locally

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `@objectstack/spec` full suite | **377 files / 9919 tests passed** |
| `@objectstack/spec` typecheck (`tsc` + scripts + test-typecheck) | **green** |
| view / view-strictness-batch18 / error-map (the card's named pins) | **129 passed** |
| `check:nul-bytes` | OK — 7063 files, no raw control bytes |
| `check:merge-driver` | green |
| `check:adr-anchors` | green |
| `check:spec-parsed-alias` | green (18 self-test assertions) |
| `check:i18n` | green after building the CLI it requires (9 packages in sync) — the first run was a **prerequisite** failure, not a drift failure |
| `check:generated` (13 artifacts) | green after regenerating **react-blocks contract** and re-running `gen:schema` / `gen:openapi` / `gen:docs`; `check:react-declaration-parity` cannot run in this repo (needs objectui's sdui manifest) |

Build closure: `@objectstack/spec` has no workspace dependencies, so the upstream-direction filter matched nothing; the package itself was built before judging `check:generated`, which reads the built dist — the first run's two "stale" artifacts included one phantom that cleared after the build.

Not run locally, by the current scoping rule: the rest of the lint farm, which CI runs once.

## Byte discipline

The smuggling check's character class covers C0 and DEL, so in the source it is written entirely as backslash-u escape sequences (u0000 through u001f, plus u007f), and the two test fixtures that feed it likewise. `node scripts/check-nul-bytes.mjs` and a wider self-scan (`grep -naP` over the C0 range) are both clean. Recording it because two raw bytes did briefly land while writing about them, and the self-scan — not the gate — is what caught them.
